quizzes.title: Liquidity and Enforcement Bodies
quizzes.passage: Banks in India need steady access to funds, and the Reserve Bank of India uses several tools to provide it. One of these is the Variable Rate Repo, which the RBI operates under its Liquidity Management Framework. The tool helps address temporary liquidity shortages in the banking system. For year-end banking stability, the RBI announced a liquidity infusion of 21.25 Lakh Crore through VRR auctions. Under this mechanism, banks borrow short-term funds from the RBI, and the process is run through auctions. The VRR is therefore a tool for temporary shortages, operated within the RBI's framework. The booklet also describes the bodies that deal with money and cyber crime. The Financial Intelligence Unit - India shares intelligence with law enforcement agencies. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre serves as the central agency for cybercrime coordination in the country. Cross-border work is led by the GlobE Network, which is designed to facilitate swift cooperation among law enforcement agencies and to recover illicit assets. Its concept grew out of the Riyadh Initiative, which was linked to Saudi Arabia's G20 Presidency.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what is the focus of the Financial Intelligence Unit - India?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists anti-money laundering as the focus of FIU-India.

questions.q: Under which convention does the GlobE Network operate?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the GlobE Network operates under the UN Convention Against Corruption.

questions.q: What duration range does the booklet give for VRR funds?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the VRR duration as 7 to 14 days.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): VRR funds are provided at fixed rates through auctions.
Reason (R): VRR funds are provided through auction-based repos.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says VRR funds come through auction-based repos rather than fixed rates, so A is false and R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Variable Rate Repo
II. Financial Intelligence Unit - India
III. Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre
IV. GlobE Network
A. Established in 2018
B. Liquidity injection tool under the Liquidity Management Framework
C. Nodal ministry is the Ministry of Finance
D. Formally launched in 2021
questions.explanation: VRR is a liquidity injection tool, FIU-India's nodal ministry is Finance, I4C was set up in 2018 and GlobE was launched in 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. FIU-India was established in 2004.
II. Banks provide government securities as collateral to borrow short-term funds from the RBI under VRR.
III. The GlobE Network concept emerged from the Riyadh Initiative in 2019.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III gives 2019 where the booklet gives 2020 for Saudi Arabia's G20 Presidency.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. FIU-India collects and analyses suspicious financial transaction reports.
2. FIU-India and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre signed an MoU to combat cyber-financial frauds.
3. The GlobE Network was formally launched in 2018.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are in the booklet, but GlobE was formally launched in 2021, not 2018.

quizzes.title: RBI Liquidity and Cyber Frauds
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India uses Variable Rate Repo auctions as a liquidity injection tool under its Liquidity Management Framework. The tool is meant for temporary liquidity shortages in the banking system. The RBI used it to ensure stability at the end of the year. Banks borrow short-term funds from the RBI, and the funds are provided through auction-based repos rather than fixed rates. Financial crime and cyber fraud are handled by specialised bodies. The Financial Intelligence Unit - India was established in 2004, and it collects and analyses suspicious financial transaction reports. It shares intelligence with law enforcement agencies and has signed an MoU with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre to combat rising cyber-financial frauds. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre serves as the central agency for cybercrime coordination in India, and it operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Cross-border cooperation is handled by the GlobE Network, which was formally launched in 2021. It is designed to facilitate swift cooperation among law enforcement agencies and to recover illicit assets, and it aims to combat transnational corruption.

questions.q: How much liquidity did the RBI infuse through VRR auctions for year-end banking stability? (in lakh crore)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the VRR liquidity infusion as 21.25 Lakh Crore.

questions.q: What is the maximum duration, in days, of VRR funds? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the VRR duration as 7 to 14 days.

questions.q: What is the nodal ministry of FIU-India? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Finance as the nodal ministry of FIU-India.

questions.q: In which year was the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre established under the Ministry of Home Affairs? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre was established in 2018.

questions.q: Under which convention does the GlobE Network operate? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the GlobE Network operates under the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, abbreviated UNCAC.

questions.q: In which year did Saudi Arabia hold the G20 Presidency whose Riyadh Initiative led to the GlobE Network concept? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet links the GlobE concept to Saudi Arabia's G20 Presidency in 2020.

questions.q: What type of securities do banks provide as collateral to borrow from the RBI under VRR? (type)
questions.explanation: The booklet says banks provide Government Securities (G-Secs) as collateral under VRR.

quizzes.title: Nutrition, Medicine and Rankings
quizzes.passage: The health and nutrition block of this booklet links nutrition policy, BRICS health cooperation and higher-education rankings. A 15-day nationwide campaign aims to drive behavioural change and improve nutritional outcomes for women and children. This campaign is one of the nutrition measures covered in the block, and it runs for a fixed 15-day period. Traditional medicine is also part of the health agenda, since the booklet describes the promotion of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine. Among the BRICS health material, the booklet describes a Health Working Group and a Mission for Healthy Lifestyles. In higher education, the booklet reports on subject-wise global rankings. These rankings draw on academic and employer reputation, along with an international research network. Indian institutions entered the marketing rankings for the first time, which indicates a shift beyond the long-standing dominance of STEM subjects. In short, the block combines a nutrition campaign, traditional medicine, BRICS health work and university rankings. Both health and higher education appear in this single block.

questions.q: Which organisation publishes the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the QS rankings are published by Quacquarelli Symonds.

questions.q: Which Indian institute leads India in Engineering and Technology in the QS subject rankings?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that IIT Delhi leads India in Engineering and Technology.

questions.q: In which year was Mission POSHAN 2.0 launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Mission POSHAN 2.0 was launched in 2021.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The BRICS Mental Health and Wellness Initiative aims to increase stigma around mental healthcare.
Reason (R): The initiative aims to strengthen mental healthcare systems and reduce stigma.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
questions.explanation: The booklet says the initiative aims to reduce stigma, so A is false and R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyles
II. Mission POSHAN 2.0
III. Integration of Traditional Medicine
IV. QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026
A. Prevention of non-communicable diseases
B. Integrated Nutrition Support System
C. AYUSH (India) systems
D. IIM Kozhikode entered the Global Top 100
questions.explanation: The booklet links the Mission to non-communicable disease prevention, POSHAN 2.0 to the Integrated Nutrition Support System, traditional medicine to AYUSH and the QS 2026 ranking to IIM Kozhikode.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India holds the 2026 BRICS Presidency.
II. The BRICS Health Working Group met in New Delhi.
III. The 15-day campaign is limited to women and children in rural areas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet supports statements I and II, while it describes the campaign for women and children with no rural limit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Citations per paper is one of the metrics used in the QS subject rankings.
2. The H-Index is one of the metrics used in the QS subject rankings.
3. The metrics include the number of Olympic medals won by each country.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 name QS metrics in the booklet, while statement 3 is not among them.

quizzes.title: Health Cooperation and Subject Rankings
quizzes.passage: The booklet's health and nutrition block covers nutrition policy, BRICS health cooperation and higher-education rankings. A 15-day nationwide campaign aims to drive behavioural change and improve nutritional outcomes for women and children, and it is one of the nutrition measures in the block. Mission POSHAN 2.0 is also part of the nutrition agenda. Traditional medicine is part of the health agenda, and the booklet describes the promotion of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine. A BRICS Mental Health and Wellness Initiative aims to strengthen mental healthcare systems, raise awareness and reduce stigma. The BRICS Health Working Group is also part of this cooperation. In higher education, the booklet reports on subject-wise global rankings. These rankings consider academic and employer reputation, citations per paper, the H-Index and an international research network. Engineering and technology is one of the subject areas in these rankings. Indian institutions have also shown a shift beyond the long-standing dominance of STEM subjects, which the booklet reads as a new trend.

questions.q: In which year was Mission POSHAN 2.0 launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Mission POSHAN 2.0 was launched in 2021 to create an Integrated Nutrition Support System.

questions.q: In which city did India host the BRICS Health Working Group meeting? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet says India hosted the BRICS Health Working Group meeting in New Delhi.

questions.q: Which institute leads India in Engineering and Technology in the QS subject rankings? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that IIT Delhi leads India in Engineering and Technology.

questions.q: Which Indian institute entered the Global Top 100 in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says IIM Kozhikode entered the Global Top 100 in the QS rankings by subject.

questions.q: What type of diseases does the BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyles focus on preventing? (phrase)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyles focuses on prevention of non-communicable diseases.

questions.q: In which year did India take up the BRICS Presidency? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India holds the 2026 BRICS Presidency.

questions.q: In which subject area did Indian institutions enter the QS rankings for the first time? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Indian institutions entered the Marketing rankings for the first time.
